Deliriuum brings together in one application a VPN tunnel, a GeckoView browser protected by Deep Shield, a search engine, direct Web browsing, and access to major social networks.
Social networks in the protected browser
When protection is active, the connection goes through a WireGuard tunnel. Websites see the IP address of the exit server instead of the usual public IP address of your connection.
DNS routed through the VPN connection
Deliriuum browsing suspended if the tunnel is lost
If the tunnel becomes unavailable, Deliriuum automatically suspends its built-in browser, search, and Web access. Other applications on the phone and their Internet access are not blocked.
Deep Shield reduces the graphical information that can be used to build a fingerprint. Sensitive WebGL rendering is hidden, and Canvas benefits from Gecko\'s anti-fingerprinting protections.
The information exposed by AudioContext is normalized to reduce differences related to audio hardware.
The set of fonts detectable by pages is greatly reduced, diminishing a common source of device identification.
Microphone and camera labels and identifiers are not exposed to pages before authorization, reducing the information available for fingerprinting.
WebRTC network candidates that could reveal information about the local network are blocked or heavily restricted.
The browser adapts certain information, particularly the time zone, to the VPN exit profile to avoid obvious inconsistencies between the visible IP address and the browser environment.
The Network Information API is not exposed to Web content, preventing the connection type, latency, or estimated bandwidth from being revealed directly.
Deliriuum relies on Gecko\'s anti-fingerprinting mechanisms and adds a consistency layer dedicated to its VPN environment.
What Deep Shield reduces or blocks
Direct exposure of your usual IP address during protected browsing
Obvious inconsistency between the VPN IP and time zone
What Deliriuum does not claim to do

Deliriuum reduces tracking and certain possibilities for correlation, but no browser can guarantee absolute anonymity. If you sign in to a personal account, the service concerned will continue to recognize you through that account. Some characteristics of the browser, network protocol, or system may also remain observable.
The project lives thanks to you
Deliriuum is free and does not rely on selling data. The project is funded by community donations, with no obligation to use the app.
MUCH MORE THAN JUST A VPN
A VPN tunnel to hide your IP address. A protected browser to reduce your digital footprint.
The VPN affects your IP address. Deep Shield affects the information that web pages can use to distinguish your device: graphics, audio, fonts, devices, network, and environment.
For security reasons, Deliriuum will send you a link to your account address. This link lets you choose a new password without exposing the old one.
This action is permanent. Confirm with your password.
An account to activate your protection
We need it to create your personal secure tunnel — like a key that only opens your door. Nothing else is required.
A confirmation link has been sent to %1$s. Click it, then come back and sign in here.
Enter your account email address. You’ll receive a secure link to choose a new password.
Can Deliriuum see my social media passwords?

No. Your password is encrypted with HTTPS directly by your device before it even leaves your phone, then passes through our WireGuard tunnel without ever being decrypted along the way — making it impossible to access, even for us. Deliriuum enforces a strict zero-logs policy: no record of your browsing is kept.

Because your privacy should never come at a price. The project is funded solely by community donations — never mandatory, never restrictive. No subscription, no time limit, and no selling data to third parties.
Does Deliriuum keep a history of my browsing?
No. No record of the sites you visit, connection times, or data usage is kept after your session.
Is it legal to use a VPN?

Yes. In France and the European Union, using a VPN is perfectly legal. Deliriuum does not facilitate any illegal activity — the app is designed to protect your privacy, not to help you circumvent the law.
What happens if I disable protection?
Social media becomes inaccessible from the app until protection is re-enabled — to prevent you from browsing without protection without realizing it.
Is the source code available for review?
Yes. The application’s source code (iOS and Android) is open source under the GPL-3.0 license. You can review it, verify it, and even contribute.
How do I delete my account?
Directly from the app, go to My account → Delete my account, then confirm with your password. Deletion is immediate and permanent — all your associated data will be erased.

Your public IP address is normally visible to the sites you visit. It can indicate your internet service provider and give an approximate idea of your location. The VPN tunnel routes your traffic through Deliriuum’s infrastructure instead of your usual connection.
Showing “connected” is not enough: you also need to verify that Internet traffic is actually passing through the tunnel. This check confirms that the protected network path is working effectively.

Your browser can sometimes indicate to the sites you visit whether you are using Wi‑Fi, a mobile network, or certain characteristics of your connection. This information does not identify you on its own, but it adds clues to your digital fingerprint.
Web pages can ask your device to perform graphics calculations with WebGL. The manufacturer, model, or behavior of the graphics chip can then become distinctive elements used to recognize a device.
Sites can test which fonts are available in your browser. The resulting combination varies depending on the system and device and can therefore add to a digital fingerprint.

Even without recording your voice or image, the browser can sometimes reveal information about the microphones, cameras, or other peripherals present. Their number, name, or identifiers can become additional clues.

WebRTC is the technology used by many sites for live audio and video calls. To establish these communications, the browser may exchange network information. If this information is too precise, it can help the sites you visit obtain additional information about your actual connection despite a VPN.
Sites can measure the logical size of the screen and its pixel density. These values can distinguish certain device families and can be combined with other characteristics to refine a fingerprint.

Your browser’s time zone provides a clue about where you are. If it indicates your actual region while your IP address appears to come from another country, the sites you visit may detect this inconsistency and infer that you are using a VPN.

The sites you visit can ask the browser to draw an invisible image and then analyze the result. Tiny differences related to the hardware, system, and graphics engine can produce a signature stable enough to contribute to fingerprinting.

The browser can process an audio signal without using your microphone. Small differences in calculations related to the hardware and software can be measured and become an additional clue for recognizing your device.

The browser can reveal general information about the platform it runs on. This data is fairly broad when considered separately, but becomes more useful for fingerprinting when combined with other clues.
A web page can ask how many logical cores your browser makes available to it. This value provides an indication of the device’s power and category and can help distinguish it from others.
The browser can indicate how many simultaneous touch points the device can handle. This characteristic helps the sites you visit better identify the type of phone or tablet being used.
This measurement checks information that web pages can observe. On its own, it does not necessarily identify your device, but it can become useful when combined with many other clues.

Settings → Security & privacy → Privacy → Permission manager → Location: remove access or disable \"Use precise location\" for non-essential apps.
Settings → Security & privacy → Privacy → More privacy settings → Ads: tap \"Delete advertising ID\".

Always enable the Deliriuum tunnel as soon as you connect to a café, train station, or hotel network. That\'s where your network packets are most vulnerable to interception.

Deliriuum uses the Android VpnService to create an encrypted tunnel between your device and our VPN infrastructure.

• Purpose: protect your internet traffic and your privacy.

• Browsing data: Deliriuum does not record your browsing history or the content of your communications, and does not sell any browsing data to third parties.

Android will then ask you for system permission before establishing the VPN tunnel.
THE APP FOR SURVIVING IN DELIRISTAN

Most VPNs only hide your IP. Deliriuum goes further: in addition to the encrypted tunnel, our Deep Shield technology modifies your device fingerprint. To social networks, you\'re no longer in Europe. No more tracking.
